## Install (no npm account needed)

```bash
npm install github:auroraxo/sememe#v0.4.10
```

```js
import { decodePayload } from 'sememe';
```

The registry name is deliberately unpublished (no name squatting): the git tag is the release artifact.

## What's in v0.4.10

- **One store answers with ONE receipt, whichever command reads it.** Measured on the published v0.4.9 install (`github:auroraxo/sememe#v0.4.9` in an empty app, no clone) with a store whose two ON-CHAIN receipts of one program carry slot strings of different digit length: `sememe decode` read the OLDER slot `99999999` and refused `sell_v3` (`unknown instruction discriminator 1c92de7726c469d5`, exit 1), while `sememe decode --union` read the newer slot `123456789` and decoded it, and `sememe lock` pinned `99999999` — a third surface, a second receipt. Two sorts, two winners: the union path has always sorted on-chain receipts by NUMERIC slot, while the plain reader and `src/lock.mjs` sorted by receipt FILENAME — and a decimal string sorts by its digits, not by its value. One comparator (`src/receipt-order.mjs`) now rules the plain reader, the union path and both lock paths: slot numerically first, filename byte-wise as tiebreak.
- **The measurement ships as an instrument, not a claim.** `tools/measure-slot-order.mjs` derives both committed artifacts — `research/slot-order-2026-11-07-before.json` (the published v0.4.9 install: 5 contract violations) and `research/slot-order-2026-11-07.json` (this tree: 0) — and `test/slot-order-measurement.test.mjs` fails if a committed report stops being what the tool derives. Nine new store tests pin the ordering (three of them RED on the pre-fix tree, plus two mutations that must each turn a test red), and the multi-copy ladder gains O6: a SECOND program with only adopted copies — plain, union and lock name the same receipt, and a damaged second copy refuses the lock and is named at verify time.
- **Reachability stated honestly.** All 44,661 live slot values across `research/` and fixtures are 9 digits (`462039125..465713413`), so two receipts written by `pull` today have equal-length slots and both orderings agree — the defect is LATENT for a fresh pull and becomes LIVE for stores whose slot strings differ in length (another era or cluster, a hand-assembled store, or mainnet crossing 1,000,000,000). The equal-length control case is green on both sides of the fix: this release changes the defective case only.

Eighth release-page note of the class this repo keeps measuring — main fixed, the pin pointing at a tag behind it: v0.4.1, v0.4.3, v0.4.4, v0.4.5, v0.4.6, v0.4.7, v0.4.8 (two verdicts from one store), now v0.4.9 (one store, two receipts, a lock pinning a third surface's pick). The instrument that measures the PUBLISHED tag itself now covers this too: the journey test installs exactly what the README pins.

## Honest limits

No external users yet (0 non-owner signals), not an audit, own-host measurement. The before/after artifacts were both measured on this host; the tag journey measures the exact bytes an install receives, but it is still one machine and my own account. The defect is latent for today's 9-digit fresh pulls (reachability above). `origin` on an adopted receipt remains a declared label, not a verified origin — honest labelling of provenance is still open. v0.4.9 keeps its behaviour (tags are immutable); its release page carries the SUPERSEDED banner pointing here.

The registry name is deliberately unpublished (no name squatting): the git tag is the release artifact.

## What's in v0.4.9

- **One store answers with ONE answer, whichever flag the caller passes.** Measured on the published v0.4.8 install (a `github:` tarball in an empty app, no clone) with a store holding two ADOPTED copies of the same pump.fun program: `sememe decode` answered `sell_v3` (fingerprint `a35349f3…`, exit 0) while `sememe decode --union` **refused the same bytes** — `unknown instruction discriminator 1c92de7726c469d5 (47 known, …)`, exit 1. Two sorts, two winners: `src/store-read.mjs` sorted adopted receipts by their LABEL (which embeds the origin the caller typed) while the plain reader and `src/lock.mjs` sorted by receipt filename (which ends in the fingerprint). One ordering rules everywhere now, copies not consulted are reported as `additionalSources`, and a three-copy store never reads as a two-source store.
- **The lock gate no longer passes over a damaged second copy.** Same measurement: `sememe lock` exited 0 and `sememe verify` reported `violations: 0` over a store whose SECOND copy had been tampered with — the README already promised "every receipt is re-checked through the store reader first, so a store the reader refuses produces NO lock, never a lock over damage", but only the NEWEST receipt per program was re-checked. `writeLock` and `checkLock` now share one verification helper, so `lock` refuses the store (exit 1, no file written) and `verify --mode error` exits 1 naming the damaged receipt.
- **The measurement ships as an instrument, not a claim.** `tools/measure-multi-copy-store.mjs` derives both artifacts — `research/multi-copy-store-2026-11-07-before.json` (the published v0.4.8 install: 7 contract violations) and `research/multi-copy-store-2026-11-07.json` (this tree: 0). Eleven new tests pin the behaviour with three mutations that must each turn a test red, and a new tag journey packs this tag and runs the same measurement against the bytes a stranger installs: red against v0.4.8 by design, green from this release on.

Seventh release-page note of the class this repo keeps measuring — main fixed, the pin pointing at a tag behind it: v0.4.1 (journey dead-ends), v0.4.3 (no lock), v0.4.4 (elided payload), v0.4.5 (peer refusal), v0.4.6 (silent typos), v0.4.7 (duplicated flag list), now v0.4.8 (two verdicts from one store, green gate over damage). The difference: this defect class now has an instrument that measures the PUBLISHED tag itself, so the next repetition fails a journey test instead of being found by reading the README.

## Honest limits

No external users yet (0 non-owner signals), not an audit, own-host measurement. The defect and the fix were measured on this host, and the tag journey measures the exact bytes an install receives — but it is still one machine and my own account. `origin` on an adopted receipt remains a declared label, not a verified origin: this release makes the label stop deciding which copy answers (the part that silently changed decode results); it does not verify the label's truth. v0.4.8 keeps its behaviour (tags are immutable); its release page carries the SUPERSEDED banner pointing here.

> **SUPERSEDED — use [v0.4.9](https://github.com/auroraxo/sememe/releases/tag/v0.4.9).**
>
> Measured 2026-11-07 against the PUBLISHED v0.4.8 install: with a store
> holding TWO adopted copies of the same pump.fun program, `sememe decode`
> answered `sell_v3` while `sememe decode --union` **refused the same bytes**
> (`unknown instruction discriminator 1c92de7726c469d5`), exit 0 vs exit 1 —
> one store, two verdicts depending on the flag. Worse, `sememe lock` exited 0
> and `sememe verify` reported `violations: 0` over that store after its
> SECOND copy had been tampered with, so the CI gate was green over damage.
> Tags are immutable, so the pin moved to v0.4.9, whose tree answers from one
> consistent copy, refuses to lock a damaged store, and names the damaged
> receipt at verify time. `test/multi-copy-store-tag-journey.test.mjs` measures
> exactly that on the PINNED tag — this tag fails it by design.

## What's in v0.4.8

- **The refusal message prints the supported flag list EXACTLY ONCE.** Measured on the published v0.4.7 install (a `github:` tarball in an empty app, no clone): for a flag with no close match the same list printed twice in one line — `sememe decode --rpc …` → `… this command accepts: --store, --trailing, --absent, --union supported flags: --store, --trailing, --absent, --union` — and a command that takes no flags printed `this command accepts: (none) supported flags: (none)`, an empty list twice. Both are now one message: `sememe decode: unknown flag "--rpc" — supported flags: --store, --trailing, --absent, --union`, and a flagless command says `this command accepts no flags`.
- **The flag level of the PINNED install is now measured, not assumed.** New `test/flag-tag-journey.test.mjs` packs this tag the way the other five journeys do and installs it into an empty app: the list prints once in both branches (F1/F2), a flagless command says so (F3), and the silent-typo class is still refused *before* any work — exit 2, no lock file, no default `~/.sememe` created (F4), with a guard on the current tree (G1). Against the v0.4.7 pin F1 and F3 were red — the defect this release heals; a mutation restoring the duplicated message turns the guard red.
- **`package-lock.json` announces the same version as `package.json` again.** Measured: a clean clone's `npm ci` reported root `0.4.1` while `package.json` said `0.4.7` (the lock had not moved since 0.4.1). Both say 0.4.8 now, and the README's test count for `test/flag-surface.test.mjs` was corrected from 28 to its actual 29.

Sixth release-page note of the class this repo keeps measuring — main fixed, the pin pointing at a tag behind it: v0.4.1 (journey dead-ends), v0.4.3 (no lock), v0.4.4 (elided payload), v0.4.5 (peer refusal), v0.4.6 (silent typos), now v0.4.7 (duplicated flag list). The difference this time: the flag level of the pin has an instrument now, so the next repetition fails a test instead of being found by running the README.

## What's in v0.4.7

- **The CLI now refuses the flags a command does not declare — before any work runs.** Until now the parser looked flags up *by name anywhere in the argument list* and dropped what it did not find, so an unknown flag was not an error but an invisible edit to the request. Measured on the published v0.4.6 install:
  - `sememe lock --store <valid> --o out.lock` → **exit 0**, lock written to `./sememe.lock`, not to `out.lock`
  - `sememe decode <prog> <payload> --stro <dir>` → the typo was dropped and the **default** `~/.sememe` was read
  - `sememe verify … --mod warn` → `--mod` dropped, verify ran in its default `error` mode
  - `sememe native-provenance --store <dir>` → the flag's **value** read as the program id
  - `sememe pull <prog> --stor <dir>` → dropped the typo and **pulled into the default store**: a write the caller never asked for
  - `--store A --store B` → the first won, the second was silently discarded
- **Each command's surface is declared as data** in `src/cli-surface.mjs` — which flags it accepts and how many positional arguments it consumes. `bin/sememe.mjs` parses the whole command line against that table *before* dispatch, so a refusal has no side effect: no store read, no file written, no RPC contacted. The refusal names the closest supported flag by measured edit distance plus the full supported list, and exits 2 (the usage channel) rather than 1 (work that failed).
- **Too few positionals are still each command's own business**, so `decode needs a program id` and `pull needs a program id` are unchanged.
- `test/flag-surface.test.mjs` (28 tests) pins it: 13 defect tests were red on the pre-fix tree with 7 guards green, and five hand mutations (unknown flag accepted, surplus positional tolerated, no suggestion, duplicate flag tolerated, missing value tolerated) each turned specific tests red before being restored byte-identical.

Fifth release-page note of the class this repo keeps measuring — main fixed, the pin pointing at a tag behind it: v0.4.1 (journey dead-ends), v0.4.3 (no lock), v0.4.4 (elided payload), v0.4.5 (peer refusal), now v0.4.6 (silent typos).

## What's in v0.4.6

- **The pinned install now refuses the missing peer in sememe's own voice.** The refusal shipped on main in `src/peer.mjs` (2026-11-06): importing `sememe/pull` or `sememe/gap` without `@solana/web3.js` throws `PeerDependencyMissingError` (code `peer_dependency_missing`) naming the package and the install command. The front-page pin still named `v0.4.5` — a tag cut BEFORE that fix, so the bytes a stranger installed still leaked Node's raw loader error while the README they read described the fixed behaviour. Measured against the PUBLISHED v0.4.5 install (peer absent, the state the optional-peer declaration puts a decoder-only consumer in):
  - `import('sememe/pull')` → `code: ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, `name: Error`, `Cannot find package '@solana/web3.js' imported from …/src/pull.mjs`
  - `import('sememe/gap')` → the same, from `…/src/acquire.mjs`
  - the CLI on that same install already refused correctly (it wraps the failure itself) — the gap was library-only, exactly what a README sentence about the library promises.
- **Fourth repetition of the "fix on main, tag behind it" class, now pinned.** v0.4.1 (journey dead-ends), v0.4.3 (no lock in the tag), v0.4.4 (elided payload) each shipped the same way. `test/acquisition-peer-surface.test.mjs` packs the working tree and could never see this.
- **`test/peer-tag-journey.test.mjs` pins the TAG, not the tree.** It packs the pinned tag the way a `github:#<tag>` install receives it, installs it into an empty app with the peer absent, and asserts: both acquisition subpaths refuse with the package AND the install command, never `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`; the tag's CLI names the instruction exactly once; and a guard test measures the current tree's tarball the same way (the one test expected green while a defective tag is still pinned). Ladder: P1/P2 red against the published v0.4.5 pin, P3 + guard green; removing `src/peer.mjs` turns the guard red, so it is not vacuous.

## What's in v0.4.5

- **A base58 payload is a payload.** The CLI has always documented "base58 or hex" for every payload argument, but the base58 path decoded to a byte array that was not a `Buffer`, and three consumers need `Buffer` methods. So the SAME bytes behaved differently depending on how they were written — measured against the PUBLISHED v0.4.4 install (a pinned install of tag `v0.4.4`), not against a working tree:
  - `sememe decode --union <program> <base58>` failed on EVERY base58 payload with `unionDecode needs the payload bytes as a Buffer`, while the same payload as hex decoded fine. The README's own union walkthrough uses a base58 payload, so it could not run.
  - an `f64`/`f32` argument died with `slice.readDoubleLE is not a function` (measured on OpenBook v2 `stubOracleCreate`, price 1.5).
  - a `bytes` argument came out as a comma-separated byte list (`1,2,3,255`) instead of base64 (`AQID/w==`) — silent corruption, not an error.
- **The fix is in three layers.** Root cause: `decodeBase58` returns a `Buffer` (a `Buffer` IS a `Uint8Array`, so every existing caller keeps working). The codec's `Cursor` normalizes its bytes to a `Buffer` once, so the shape of the input cannot decide whether it decodes. The union path normalizes instead of refusing, and still refuses input that is not a byte array at all.
- **`test/base58-payload-bytes.test.mjs` pins the equality.** For each of the three cases, the base58 form and the hex form must produce the same instruction, the same fields and the same verdict — plus the CLI end to end. Two mutations (revert `decodeBase58`; remove the `Cursor` guard) must turn the contract red, so the guards are not decorative. Suite: 515 tests, 513 pass, 2 named-skip, 0 fail.

The section now documents the store-creating `pull` BEFORE the commands that need the store, in both the clone and the install form.
- `test/lock-journey.test.mjs` pins both: L1 runs the pinned tag's own documented lock journey from the packed tarball against the committed fixture store; L2 refuses a lock section whose store-consuming command has no pull command before it; G1 guards main.

## What's in v0.4.2

- **The pinned tag's OWN README now runs the consumer journey.** Measured on the packed `v0.4.1` tarball (2026-11-05): the consumer section had no `pull` command, so the first decode died with `no sememe store at ./store: run "sememe pull" first`; and the only invocation form that works from an install (`npx sememe`) appeared 0 times — bare `sememe` is not on `PATH` after a plain `npm install`, and `node bin/sememe.mjs` resolves only inside a clone. `v0.4.1`'s README could not be fixed (tags are immutable), so the pin moved here, where the shipped README documents `npx sememe pull` / `npx sememe decode` verbatim.

The tag is resolved locally or fetched from origin; if it is not published, the test skips with that reason instead of measuring a different tree.
- The install pins point at `v0.4.2`, whose tree ships everything the README documents (`sememe gap`, `sememe/raydium`, `sememe/token-metadata`).
